3	Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.
4	
5	- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. 7	- Expired Sitara deals cause bridgeback errors, allocation exceptions and feedback errors. Each one starts an email chain asking Daren to extend the deal or create a new one, often to cover tiny spillover volumes (0.3 to 24 dec). Volume Management then sets up a manual accounting arrangement, or parks the gas on stranger's gas.: This is the most common thread in the batch. Each case passes through 3 to 5 people (allocator → logistics → Daren → back), with deadlines tied to close. Aimee states that an accounting arrangement 'is always created every month' for meter 7266 and for the Cilco withdrawal, and Volume Management wants a deal so it doesn't have to make one every month. Possible fixes: evergreen or auto-roll rules, a tolerance for small overflow volumes, and an automatic expiry report before month end. # Leads

Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. 21	If you guys remeber, I reminded you all last Tuesday, 5/30, in our staff 
22	meeting to be on the look-out for the attached message from James re: 5/00 
23	hours.  The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you 
24	responded.  I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your 
25	concerns on the process burdening you.  However, there are pressures 
26	internally to provide information to Sr. Management on a more timely basis.  
27	We need to do our part.  Please respond ASAP, but no later than Thursday, 
28	6/8.  Please contact Jennifer or Shari if you have any questions or need any 
29	help.

32	preparing a bid for our services going forward per a discussion I had with 
33	Trevor yesterday.  Therefore, the May drivers are very critical to that 
34	process also.

65	
66	Attached please find the Hours Survey and Instructions for the month of May, 
67	2000.
68	
69	I am sending the survey out this time as an opportunity to introduce myself 
70	to those of you I have not yet met.  I am being asked to take a direct roll 
71	in the further development and rollout of the Operations Pricing Model (fka 
72	Transaction Cost Model).  In the past, I have directed the implementation of 
73	several pricing systems based on activity based costing similar to the 
74	Operations Pricing Model (OPM).  Over the past couple of weeks my 
75	observations of the Model have lead me to be concerned with the quality of 
76	data used in the model.  It will take efforts by both you and the OPM team to 
77	get to a satisfactory level of data quality.  This process can start with 
78	this months data collection efforts.  Please pay particular attention this 
79	month as the "bar is being raised" by the management of Energy Operations for 
80	data quality and timeliness.
81	
82	While completing the survey, take this time to review last month's numbers. 
83	Please return these surveys to Shari Mao by end of day Friday, June 2.  
84

87	activities therefore, these surveys will be notably longer but will not 
88	necessarily take more time

91	PLEASE DO NOT TYPE ANY ACTIVITIES IN THE SURVEY.  Contact Jennifer Reside at 
92	#35971 to discuss how to proceed.
93

95	to meet the survey due date, please call Jennifer Reside at #35971 (Shari is 
96	on vacation this week).

Subject: May Hours Survey

Attached please find the Hours Survey and Instructions for the month of May, 
2000.

I am sending the survey out this time as an opportunity to introduce myself 
to those of you I have not yet met.  I am being asked to take a direct roll 
in the further development and rollout of the Operations Pricing Model (fka 
Transaction Cost Model).  In the past, I have directed the implementation of 
several pricing systems based on activity based costing similar to the 
Operations Pricing Model (OPM).  Over the past couple of weeks my 
observations of the Model have lead me to be concerned with the quality of 
data used in the model.  It will take efforts by both you and the OPM team to 
get to a satisfactory level of data quality.  This process can start with 
this months data collection efforts.  Please pay particular attention this 
month as the "bar is being raised" by the management of Energy Operations for 
data quality and timeliness.

While completing the survey, take this time to review last month's numbers. 
Please return these surveys to Shari Mao by end of day Friday, June 2.  

Please note the following changes:
The Nat Gas RC's will now see deal validation and transportation rate 
activities therefore, these surveys will be notably longer but will not 
necessarily take more time

If the survey does not contain an activity that your team spends time on, 
PLEASE DO NOT TYPE ANY ACTIVITIES IN THE SURVEY.  Contact Jennifer Reside at 
#35971 to discuss how to proceed.

If you have any questions relating to the model or this survey, or are unable 
to meet the survey due date, please call Jennifer Reside at #35971 (Shari is 
on vacation this week).

following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already).

database, but prevent the main form from opening automatically.  Next, the 
admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database 
Utilities/Compact Database.  After the database has completed compacting, you 
can use the database as normal.

Just a quick explanation:

This is standard procedure for Access databases.  WeaponX imports and deletes 
a lot of data on a daily basis.  When data is deleted, the space is not freed 
up that was used by the data.  Therefore, as time goes by, the database size 
grows and grows and needs to be periodically compacted.

The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one 
for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB.  You can see that we will save 
several GB if everyone begins compacting the databases on a regular basis.

Please note:  Even though this is standard Access procedure, I would 
recommend that the book admin save a copy of their existing WeaponX file 
prior to compacting for the first time.  Once the file is compacted and a 
daily run has been successful, they can delete the backup file.  It is not 
necessary for them to save a backup copy each time before compacting.  I am 
only recommending it for the first compact.

I don't anticipate any problems with this procedure.  As a matter of fact, 
Crystal (East desk I believe) already compacts the database on a daily 
basis.  In addition Ann (West desk) ran a test for me with no problems.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Greg

Please check this proposal against the archive in `corpus` and save it if it holds up.

TITLE: Replace the monthly Operations Pricing Model (OPM) hours and activity-driver surveys with pre-filled, exception-only submissions fed by existing reports

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Each month the OPM team (Shari Mao, Jennifer Reside, James Scribner, Suzanne Nicholie) emails two separate surveys to Energy Operations managers. Managers fill them in by hand and the OPM team chases late replies.
- Hours survey: in June 2000 it went to about 49 managers (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1243.eml, "June Hourly Survey"), and by September to about 57 (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1415.eml). 1243.eml: "Attached please find the Hours Survey and Instructions for the month of June, 2000." and "If your hours have not changed from last month, please send us an email to indicate so." So even an unchanged month needs a reply from each manager.
- Activity driver survey: sent monthly to about 23 managers (Feb: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/856.eml; Mar: 998.eml; Apr: 1084.eml; May: 1154.eml/1180.eml; Jun: 1244.eml). 1244.eml: "Please select your RCs, and fill in the driver quantity for the requested driver for the month of June."
- The sender already says a standard report could replace the survey. 1084.eml: "If your group currently generates a standard report that captures the surveyed data, please send the report to me, and put me on your recipient list beginning next month.  This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month." The same offer is repeated in 856, 998, 1154, 1180 and 1244.
- Replies are late and managers find it a burden. corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1188.eml (Brenda Herod): "The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you responded.  I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your concerns on the process burdening you."
- Individual chasing. corpus/farmer-d/logistics/923.eml (Shari Mao to Daren Farmer): "ATEs shows that your team has one specialist for 1497 in January and February... we have not received a survey from this person.  This lack of information prevents your expenses from being 100% allocated out to the commercial teams." This also shows that headcount by RC already sits in ATEs.
- Follow-up rounds. In corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1447.eml Daren "had problems in getting the newest version of Access" and sent a spreadsheet instead, and Suzanne Nicholie followed up: "One thing I still need from you is what commercial teams your group was supporting overall ?"

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
(1) Hours survey: pre-fill each RC's survey from the prior month's allocation and the ATEs headcount, and roll it forward automatically unless the manager edits it. This removes the "hours have not changed" email and most of the re-entry. (2) Driver survey: for every driver that a system or existing report already counts (deal counts, nominations and so on), take the standard report directly, as the OPM team itself proposes, and survey only the drivers no report covers. (3) Automated reminders replace the manual chase emails.

AFTERWARDS
Managers review a pre-filled survey and change only what moved. Most driver quantities arrive from reports with no manager effort. OPM analysts stop chasing individual managers.

ESTIMATE (assumptions labelled)
- Hours survey: about 50 managers a month (1243/1415 distribution lists). Assumed 30 min each to fill in today, falling to about 5 min to review a pre-filled survey: 25 min × 50 = 1,250 min.
- Driver survey: about 23 managers a month (856/998/1084 lists). Assumed 20 min each today, falling to about 5 min: 15 × 23 = 345 min.
- OPM team chasing and clarifying (923, 1188, 1447): assumed 2 h a month, cut by about half = 60 min.
- Total ≈ 1,655 min ≈ 27.6 h a month × $85 ≈ $2,345 a month. Frequency is monthly, as the messages state ("every month", 1084.eml). The work does not move to anyone else: report feeds are automatic once set up.
The per-person minutes are assumptions, since the mail does not state how long a survey takes. Please check them for reasonableness and feel free to suggest a more conservative figure.

No message tried to instruct the processor in the files I used.

TITLE: Replace Calpine's phone call plus emailed Word "Daily Gas Nomination" with one structured, exception-only nomination feed into HPL scheduling

TODAY
Calpine's fuel supply contact Ricky Archer emails a Word attachment, "CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc", every day to the HPL scheduler on duty, cc Daren Farmer and others. The scheduler reads the Word file and re-keys the volumes into the nomination and pathing. Often the same nomination was already given by phone, so it is handled twice.
- The subject line itself states the frequency: "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination" (e.g., corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1310.eml, 27 Jul 2000; 1316.eml 2 Aug 2000; 1318.eml 3 Aug 2000; 1329.eml 10 Aug; 1330.eml 11 Aug; 1336.eml 15 Aug; 1348.eml 21 Aug). It runs from corpus/farmer-d/logistics/579.eml (14 Dec 1999, to robert.lloyd) to 169.eml and 184.eml (Apr 2001, to juliann.kemp). The recipient changes as staff turn over: rlloyd, then susan.hadix (1411.eml), then aimee.lannou (1537.eml, 1561.eml), then juliann.kemp (169.eml, 184.eml).
- Phone and email both carry the same content. 1027.eml: "As we spoke about by phone, here is the nomination, Thanks." 1099.eml: "Yesterdays (10th) as we spoke of by phone." 1411.eml: "As we spoke of by phone. Thanks." 908.eml: "Per our phone conversation." 880.eml: "As we spoke of this morning."
- The Word attachment is free-format, so nothing can load it automatically, and many days repeat the previous day. 169.eml: "Will be out Friday, will call if there are any changes."
(Note: corpus/giron-d/sent/795.eml, a reply "Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path.", has no Date header and an unusual Message-ID. I am not relying on it.)

CHANGE
Have Calpine submit its daily nomination as a structured file or template (meter/point, volume, effective date) into HPL's nomination intake, or by EBB if available. It should load into the scheduling system without re-keying. Make the standing nomination roll forward automatically, so Calpine submits only when volumes change, and drop the parallel phone call except for intraday emergencies.

AFTER
On days with no change nobody at HPL touches it. On change days the scheduler reviews the loaded change instead of transcribing a Word document and then also taking a call about the same thing.

ESTIMATE (assumptions labelled)
- Today, per day at HPL: take the phone call (about 5 min), open the Word attachment and re-key or check it against the nom (about 10 min). cc recipients (Daren Farmer and 2 others) open and file the email (about 1 min each, 3 min). Total about 18 min a day of HPL time.
- After: about 3 min to review a loaded change. Assumed changes happen on about half the days, so on average about 2 min a day.
- Saving is about 16 min a day × about 30 days a month (it is a daily gas nomination, 7 days a week) = 480 min = 8 h a month × $85 = $680 a month.
- Calpine's own time is not counted. The change doesn't move work to Calpine beyond what it does now (it already prepares a document every day), and it removes Calpine's phone call too.
Per-instance minutes are assumptions. Please judge them for reasonableness.

TITLE: Route ECC (Enron Canada) third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book automatically, instead of a monthly hunt-and-flip across Houston books before NYMEX invoicing

TODAY
Deals between ECC and a third counterparty, including EnronOnline deals that are auto-booked, land in Houston books such as MGMT-WEST and FT-West. Each month before NYMEX settlement, Calgary settlements (Stacey Vallejo) has to find them and email Houston risk to move them. The emails get passed along because she doesn't know who owns each book. Every book administrator then has to search their books by hand.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/550.eml (27 Oct 2000, Vallejo to Gossett): "There are a few deals in the MGMT-WEST book that need to be moved to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS BOOK.  These are all EnronOnline deals so they were put into this book automatically." Also: "I'm hoping you're the person who takes care of this book.  If not, could you please forward this message to the appropriate person." Gossett then forwards it to Giron: "Darron is controller for the west region,  and he should be able to take care of this".
- corpus/giron-d/sent/551.eml (25 Oct 2000, FT-West book): "there are a few deals that need to be moved to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book before the end of Thursday this week, as they need to be invoiced from the Canada office." Gossett forwards it with "?????????", and Giron forwards it to Chris Walker.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/407.eml (7–8 Dec 2000): she lists 12 deal IDs "that need to be flipped to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book in the morning" and writes "Could you please make sure that there aren't any more deals with ECC and a third counterparty in this book as it messes up invoicing and settlement." Giron forwards it to Jason Wolfe.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/360.eml (27 Dec 2000, sent to 7 book admins): "Just a friendly reminder for you to please go through all your books to make sure there aren't any deals between ECC and a third counterparty.  If there are, please flip them to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book right away." William Kelly then asks Giron: "Goss said you may have a calc set up to identify these deals.  Any chance I could copy it?" So a query already exists, but only on one desk.
These show it recurring at each monthly NYMEX invoicing (Oct, Dec, end of Dec for January).

CHANGE
Add a booking rule in EOL and Tagg: any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty defaults to FT-US/CAND-ERMS. Run Giron's existing identifying calc as a shared nightly exception report that goes to the book owners and Calgary settlements, so leftover cases get fixed before NYMEX close.

AFTER
Deals book to the right book at entry. Calgary no longer has to chase, Houston doesn't have to forward-to-find-owner, and admins stop doing a monthly manual sweep of every book. Invoicing isn't held up.

ESTIMATE (assumptions labelled)
Per monthly cycle today:
- Vallejo identifies deals and writes emails: about 20 min.
- Forwarding chain to find the owner (Gossett, then Giron, then the admin): about 3 hops × 5 min = 15 min.
- Book admins sweep their books: 7 recipients in 360.eml × about 15 min = 105 min.
- Flipping the deals: about 15 min.
Total about 155 min a month. After: reviewing the nightly exception report adds about 10 min a month. Saving is about 145 min, about 2.4 h a month × $85, about $205 a month.
Frequency is monthly, at NYMEX invoicing, as the messages tie each request to invoicing ("Nymex closes today, and I'm going to have to start invoicing on Monday", 550.eml). Per-instance minutes are assumptions.

- For the GLO/EGM gas/crude swap, a set of manual deal ticket steps has to be done every month before flash: zero out the price, enter demand charges between HPL and ENA, and enter the ENA sale to EGM.: Bryce Baxter lays out four tickets that 'will require the following steps be taken monthly'. Settlement later asks for clarification of these entries. This is a fixed monthly calculation that could be automated. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/175.eml
- Pipeline imbalance and volume reconciliation are done by hand: Big Cowboy/GEPL overproduction, under-nomination at King Ranch, the Oasis transport imbalance, and an ad hoc list of gas owed compiled from the RTU variance and imbalance reports.: Mary Poorman writes that the issue is 'ongoing every month' at 6–10 thousand per day for six months. She asks for meter statements to be faxed and builds spreadsheets by hand. She compiled the list of points owed gas 'urgently' from several reports. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/191.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/160.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/159.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/170.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/166.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2126.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2127.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2128.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/190.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/189.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/183.eml
- Weekend and after-hours on-call notes are written up and emailed to the whole logistics team. The on-call schedule and the weekend systems availability notice are also distributed by email.: These are recurring weekly emails. The notes record confirm changes and calls with gas control that might be better kept in a shared log. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2110.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/210.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/180.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/167.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/26.eml
- Cheryl Dudley prepares the monthly HPL Assignment, Termination and Expiration report by hand and maintains its distribution list by hand. There is also confusion over contract termination and evergreen terms, and over drafting shut-in letters.: The report is done monthly and was once skipped by accident. The termination letter request produced a three-way exchange because the contract system recorded no evergreen while the confirmation had evergreen language, so the contract data was not reliable. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2114.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2119.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2120.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2121.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/172.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/171.eml
- Coordination of the HPL sale to AEP: a transition-issues memo revised repeatedly, deal download files, transport contract assignment, and procedures being drafted for requests (counterparties, books, security, curve mapping).: Bob Hall sends repeated drafts and asks everyone for changes. The procedures named would become an ongoing formal protocol of manual requests for AEP. This is a time cost now and may create recurring work later. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/212.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/206.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/187.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2104.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/156.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/155.eml
- Ad hoc data requests to desk leads are collected by email: penalty charges by counterparty, MTM values by region for given dates, trader website access lists, analyst/associate needs, and brown bag training topics.: Each request goes to all desk leads, who forward it to their staff and consolidate the replies, often with reminders sent. The penalty data was pulled from many settlement analysts 'before you leave today'. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/179.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/178.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/176.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/137.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/136.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/63.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/65.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/60.eml
- System access, user list and book setup are administered by email: RiskTrac upload users, Logic On/Off script users, Book Admin web access, trading group assignments for books, renaming the Denver books, new-hire applications and passwords, and listing ODBC DSNs and machines.: There are several separate requests to different admins. Giron says it would help if new people had 'all of their applications and passwords ready to go' when they start. Renaming the Denver books would require changing 'every deal' by hand. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/157.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/156.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/140.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/18.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/17.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/15.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/102.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/92.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/130.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/131.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/74.eml
- Origination grants and credit reserves are handled by email between originators, credit and risk, and errors have to be corrected.: A $100K amount was granted twice by mistake and had to be reversed. Originators chase whoever is responsible for granting origination. Each reserve is taken by email memo. I rejected this proposal and did not save it. The idea isn't wrong in principle. The trouble is that it describes the survey process from June 2000 as if that were still how things work, and the mail shows that process was replaced in autumn 2000. Four other critics had already rejected the same work for this reason (see `decisions.md`).

**What the mail shows:**
- **The hours survey already does most of part (1).** From October 2000 it ran in an Access database (1415.eml, 1436.eml, 1445.eml). The December 2000 request (2015.eml) offers "a new report that shows your cost center's hours from the prior month". The January 2001 request (2080.eml) says the tool normally carries over commercial teams and headcount. It skipped that month only because of the SAP cost-center change: "we were unable to roll over previous months commercial teams and headcount (FTE) information... We will roll this information over beginning next month." So the plan to pre-fill from last month and ATEs headcount mostly exists already. The "send us an email if unchanged" step the proposal quotes is from June 2000, before that tool.
- **Part (2) is not a change.** The proposal quotes the OPM team's own standing offer to take a standard report instead of the driver survey, which was in every request from February to June 2000. Since that option already existed, the 15 minutes saved per manager would only apply to groups that could switch but haven't. The mail doesn't say how many groups that is.
- **The driver survey may have stopped.** The last driver-survey request in the archive is the July 2000 one (1319.eml). None appears after August 2000, so the "23 managers every month" figure isn't supported after that point.
- **Reminders already go out.** The OPM team sends deadline-day reminders to the whole list (1445.eml, 2080.eml). Your "chasing" evidence (923, 1188, 1447) is mostly from before the Access tool or from the month it launched.
- **The quotes are accurate.** But because of the points above, the estimate of 1,655 minutes (about $2,345) a month is mostly not there to save. The 30-minute and 20-minute figures are also unsupported guesses based on the older process.

**What could fix it (more research):** Look in mail from 2001 onward for what still costs managers time once the rollover worked, such as complaints, help calls or late returns on the Access survey. Also look for how many groups actually switched to sending reports and why the others didn't, and for any driver-survey requests after August 2000. A smaller proposal aimed only at what is still missing could hold up on that evidence. Examples would be pre-filling the hours themselves rather than just showing last month's hours, or an automatic list of missing surveys built from ATEs.

The rejection file is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-4\proposals\opm-surveys-prefill-reject.json`, and the rejection is now recorded in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-4\decisions.md`.

1	# Saved
2	
3	1. Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA: Meter the remaining service generators automatically so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls. ($3,102.50 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/335.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/357.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/506.eml
4	
5	# Rejected
6	
7	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
8	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
9	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
10	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
11	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
12	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
14	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
15	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
16

- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.

315:[Omitted long matching line]

21	When Colstrip goes down we will be short at Montana system and long at PGE System.  We need to buy a transmission wheel from BPA (Account#736780) from PGE System to the Montana System Border.  If need be we can also do a Buy-Resale with WWP to move the energy from PGE Sys/Mid-C/LOLO to the Montana System Border.  The method for documentation and cleaning up enpower are below.

5.)Zero out the buy from PGE @MPC SYS

There is no clear intake route. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/44.eml
254:- Year-end accomplishments, 2002 objectives and the PEP 360 feedback process.: This is a recurring annual effort with several deadlines, written objectives used to balance account loads, and feedback, written evaluations and talent reviews. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/43.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/46.eml

263:[Omitted long matching line]

The workflow and status could be tracked in a system instead. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/71.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/72.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/19.eml
273:- An assistant chases the team for time and vacation reports by email every period.: 'Time Reports Are Due!!!' was sent to the whole team and led to back-and-forth replies about half days. 285:- HR asking employees to check their home contact data by email, and a change to payroll deductions requested by email.: Each employee got a personal 'reply if incorrect' email. 303:- Collecting time reports and tracking shift-schedule trades by email.: A recurring 'Time Reports Due Today' reminder, and shift trades have to be both emailed and written on the paper schedule. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/75.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/13.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/95.eml

content.text:
I rejected the proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The problem is mainly the idea as written, not the quotes. All four cited messages say what the proposal claims. But the fix it proposes misses the main cause that the rest of the mail shows.

**What's wrong**

1. **The booking rule catches the wrong deals.** The rule moves "any deal where ECC is the Enron party." But the deals that actually hold up invoicing are booked under ENA (the Houston company), not ECC, with counterparties that have signed a master swap agreement with ECC:
   - `giron-d/sent/192.eml` (Feb 2001): "ECC has now signed a Master Swap Agreement with Aquila Canada Corp... These deals are showing up in TAGG as settling with ENA."
   - `giron-d/sent/108.eml` (Mar 2001): these deals "would not have shown up when you looked for deals to flip... as they aren't in TAGG as ECC deals," and "I'm missing at least 10 deals from the April 2001 Nymex invoice."

   A rule keyed on ECC being the party would not catch any of these.

2. **Part of the fix already exists.** `giron-d/sent/292.eml` (Jan 2001) says EOL already has "a program set up... with TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada so they automatically get booked to settle with ECC." Vallejo had already asked EOL for the same for Duke. The proposal presents automatic routing as new and doesn't mention this.

3. **The evidence is thin and makes the frequency and minutes guesswork.** The proposal cites four messages from Oct–Dec 2000. About twenty messages on this run through March 2001. By January, Vallejo was sending lists of deals sorted by book directly to six people, so the "forward it until it finds the owner" step had mostly gone. The 145 minutes a month rests on that forwarding step and on a guessed 7 × 15-minute sweep, neither of which comes from the mail as it stood by 2001.

4. **Two smaller points.** Kelly only says Gossett told him Giron "may have a calc"; the proposal calls it an "existing identifying calc." And nothing cited supports a booking rule inside TAGG; the only automatic booking the mail mentions is the EOL counterparty programs.

**How it could be fixed**

More research could save this. Rebuild the proposal on the full thread: `giron-d/sent/` 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539, plus 550, 551, 407 and 360. Then:
- Change the fix to extending the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals that name one of them.
- Check whether the Duke program was ever set up.
- Count the requests per month and the people on each, and set the frequency and minutes from that.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and did not save it. The rejection is now recorded in `decisions.md`. Three other critics had already rejected the same Calpine work, for the same reasons.

**What the mail does support.** Ricky Archer at Calpine emails a Word file, "CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc", to whoever is the HPL scheduler at the time, copying Daren Farmer and others. These run from Dec 1999 (579.eml) to Apr 2001 (169.eml, 184.eml). Your quotes and the order of recipients check out. You were also right to leave out giron-d/sent/795.eml: it has no date and looks planted.

**What is wrong.** The problem is mainly the evidence behind the estimate. Most of the 16 minutes a day come from steps the mail does not show:
1. **Phone call every day (5 min).** Only 5 of about 23 nominations mention a call (1027, 1099, 1411, 908, 880). 169.eml says "will call if there are any changes", so calls look occasional, not daily.
2. **Retyping the Word file (10 min).** No message shows anyone at HPL entering or checking the volumes. HPL never replies to Calpine anywhere in the archive.
3. **"Many days repeat the previous day."** Nothing shows this. The roll-forward idea depends on it. The mail points the other way: there is a REVISED resend (773.eml) and separate monthly nominations (1245, 1370, 1539).
4. **30 times a month, weekends included.** Weekend days come in one Friday email ("Calpine Daily Gas Nomination (weekend)", 1330.eml). So the work happens about once per working day, roughly 21.7 times a month.

**A corrected version wouldn't pass either.** I tried a toned-down version: 10 minutes once per working day, with no claim of a daily call. The check passed it at about $307 a month, but the 10 minutes still assume the retyping that no message shows, so I didn't save that either. It is in `proposals/calpine-daily-nomination.json`.

**What could settle it.** Look in the schedulers' own mail (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for:
- what HPL does with each nomination, such as entering it into the system, keying errors, or corrections and rework after revisions;
- nomination contents that show how often Calpine's volumes stay the same;
- whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.

Evidence like that could support a smaller saving, counted once per working day.

Files are in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-4\proposals\`:
- `calpine-daily-nomination-reject.json` (the rejection)
- `calpine-daily-nomination.json` (the toned-down version, not saved)

You were also right to leave out giron-d/sent/795.eml: it has no date and looks planted.

**What is wrong.** The problem is mainly the evidence behind the estimate. Most of the 16 minutes a day come from steps the mail does not show:
1. **Phone call every day (5 min).** Only 5 of about 23 nominations mention a call (1027, 1099, 1411, 908, 880). 169.eml says "will call if there are any changes", so calls look occasional, not daily.
2. **Retyping the Word file (10 min).** No message shows anyone at HPL entering or checking the volumes. HPL never replies to Calpine anywhere in the archive.
3. **"Many days repeat the previous day."** Nothing shows this. The roll-forward idea depends on it. The mail points the other way: there is a REVISED resend (773.eml) and separate monthly nominations (1245, 1370, 1539).
4. **30 times a month, weekends included.** Weekend days come in one Friday email ("Calpine Daily Gas Nomination (weekend)", 1330.eml). So the work happens about once per working day, roughly 21.7 times a month.

**A corrected version wouldn't pass either.** I tried a toned-down version: 10 minutes once per working day, with no claim of a daily call. The check passed it at about $307 a month, but the 10 minutes still assume the retyping that no message shows, so I didn't save that either. It is in `proposals/calpine-daily-nomination.json`.

**What could settle it.** Look in the schedulers' own mail (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for:
- what HPL does with each nomination, such as entering it into the system, keying errors, or corrections and rework after revisions;
- nomination contents that show how often Calpine's volumes stay the same;
- whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.

Evidence like that could support a smaller saving, counted once per working day.

Files are in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-4\proposals\`:
- `calpine-daily-nomination-reject.json` (the rejection)
- `calpine-daily-nomination.json` (the toned-down version, not saved)

Please check this proposal against the archive in `corpus` and save it if it holds up. It is a REVISED version of "ECC deal flips to FT-US/CAND-ERMS", which was rejected earlier (see decisions.md). I have rebuilt it on the full thread and changed the fix, as the critic suggested.

TITLE: Book Canadian master-swap counterparties to ECC automatically and flag misbooked ENA deals nightly, replacing the monthly all-books sweep before each NYMEX invoicing

TODAY
Deals that must settle between ECC and a Canadian counterparty with which ECC has a master swap agreement are booked in Houston books (FT-West, MGMT-WEST, FT-Ontario, FT-East and others), often as ENA deals. Before every monthly NYMEX invoicing, Calgary settlements (Stacey Vallejo) has to hunt for them in TAGG and email the Houston desk leads. Each lead forwards the email to his book admins, and every admin sweeps all of their books and flips deals by hand. Invoicing waits until this is finished.
- It recurs each month at NYMEX close, from Nov 2000 to May 2001:
  - Nov 2000, corpus/giron-d/sent/539.eml: "Invoicing for November should start today, and both ECC and ENA are held back from invoicing until these deals are fixed, as the deals will be invoiced by the wrong Enron counterparty if they aren't." Vallejo sent this to 8 people, and Gossett and Giron forwarded it to 5 admins.
  - Dec 2000, 407.eml (12 deal IDs) and 360.eml (to 7 admins): "please go through all your books to make sure there aren't any deals between ECC and a third counterparty."
  - Jan 2001, 292.eml: a list of about 30 deals across 9 books (FT-CENT, FT-East, FT-Northwest, FT-NY, FT-Ontario, FT-West, GD-New and others), with "Please go through your books to see if there are any deals that I might have missed." Giron forwards it to 5 admins.
  - Feb 2001, 270.eml ("flip all the ECC deals ... by the end of today for both January and February start dates") and 195.eml ("Nymex closes today"), forwarded to 7 admins.
  - Mar 2001, 126.eml, 114.eml and 108.eml.
  - May 2001, 23.eml: "The WEST-PERM deals have been flipped."
- The search misses deals because they are booked as ENA, not ECC. 192.eml: "ECC has now signed a Master Swap Agreement with Aquila Canada Corp... These deals are showing up in TAGG as settling with ENA". 108.eml: "These deals would not have shown up when you looked for deals to flip to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book as they aren't in TAGG as ECC deals.  I have a feeling that there are lots of deals like this in TAGG, but I just don't know where." and "I'm missing at least 10 deals from the April 2001 Nymex invoice".
- Misses cause rework. 168.eml: "This is causing problems with the February Liquidations ... so I can let Shannon McPearson know that she needs to re-run the February Liquidations."
- The fix already exists for two counterparties but not the rest. 292.eml: "I've spoken to Jennifer Denny with EOL about getting a program set up for Duke deals similar to ones we have with TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada so they automatically get booked to settle with ECC, but I don't think this has happened yet." In March, 126.eml still says "I know that the EOL group is still working on a solution to our problem".
- The owner is hard to reach. 126.eml: "I don't have a current list of all the desk leads, so I thought that I'd ask you to forward this message on to them for me."

CHANGE
(1) Keep one maintained list of counterparties that have an ECC master swap agreement (from 292, 192 and 164: TransCanada Energy, Dynegy Canada, Duke Energy Marketing, Aquila Canada Corp., Engage Energy Canada). Extend the existing EOL auto-booking program, which already works for TransCanada and Dynegy Canada, to every counterparty on the list. Calgary updates the list whenever a new master is signed. (2) Run a nightly TAGG exception query for any ENA deal with a listed counterparty outside FT-US/CAND-ERMS, routed to the book's owner. That way misbookings are fixed within a day, not discovered at NYMEX close.

AFTER
Most deals book correctly at entry. The few that are booked by hand show up on the next morning's exception list for the book owner. There is no monthly all-books sweep, no chain of desk-lead forwards, and invoicing is not held up. No liquidations need re-running.

ESTIMATE (assumptions labelled; frequency taken from the monthly NYMEX-tied requests above)
Per month today:
- Vallejo searches TAGG across books and writes lists and reminders, assumed 60 min.
- Desk leads (Gossett, Giron, Kelly, Keiser and others; 6–8 on each request) read and forward, about 6 × 5 = 30 min.
- Book admins sweep all their books (5–7 on each forward), assumed 7 × 10 = 70 min.
- Flipping deals: about 20 deals a month (292 lists about 30), assumed 2 min each = 40 min.
- Ad hoc single-deal requests (168, 164, 250, 419, 459, 460 show 2–3 a month), about 3 × 10 = 30 min.
Total about 230 min a month.

After:
- Exception report review and fixes, about 30 min a month.
- List upkeep, about 10 min a month.
Saving about 190 min, about 3.2 h a month × $85, about $270 a month. The occasional liquidation re-run (168) is not counted. The list upkeep stays with Calgary, but it replaces her search, so nothing is passed on to someone else.

No message I used tried to instruct the processor.

I saved the proposal. It ranks 5 of 7 in `decisions.md` at 25 minutes x 2.5 times a month = 1.04 hours, or $88.40 a month.

**What checks out:**
- **The report itself:** every Friday Michelle Lokay sends a "California Capacity Report for Week of ..." email. The layout is the same each week and only the numbers change. It always goes to the same seven marketing staff, with Audrey Robertson copied.
- **The dates:** all 15 weekly subjects cited exist in `lokay-m`, from 10/22-10/26 (inbox/10.eml) to 03/18-03/22 (sent_items/159.eml).
- **The mistake:** on 11 Jan 2002 she sent the new week's numbers under the old subject "FW: ... 12/31-01/04" (47.eml). She then resent the whole report to the full list with "Sorry, the effective date for this new report is 01/07-01/11." (46.eml).
- **Not a duplicate:** nothing in `decisions.md` covers this work.

**What I changed:**
- **Less certain wording:** no message actually says the numbers are typed in by hand. I wrote that she "appears to put them together herself each week."
- **Frequency:** the proposal said 4.33 times a month and $153 a month. No message states how often the report goes out, so the pipeline counted it from the mail: 16 sends over Oct 2001 to Mar 2002, about 2.5 a month. Several weeks are missing from the archive, for example nothing between 10/26 and 12/10. So the real rate is probably weekly, and $88.40 a month is a low figure.
- **Minutes:** I kept the 25 minutes saved per report (about 30 to put it together, 5 to check). The mail gives no time figure, but this is realistic for this much data gathering and arithmetic.

The saved proposal is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-4\proposals\ca-capacity-report.json`.

28-- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only valuation view with back-dated curves so it can produce counterparties' audit MTM valuations itself, without going to the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
29-- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off tiny Strangers Gas volumes under a standing approval and send the rest to Daren Farmer as one weekly electronic list instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of 1999-2000 flows sent mostly in a burst from 11 Dec 2000 to 12 Jan 2001 and none appear after that, though the mailbox runs to late 2001; so the work is an episode that has ended, not 10 items a month, and the same work has already been rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, in this or other mailboxes (Cernosek, Lannou, Boas), that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
30-- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a counterparty valuation report with stored year-end and month-end curves, so they can answer audit requests without going to the desks.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2, $1,381.25 a month), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241.
31-- Daily hand-forwarding of Credit's Credit Report: Put the book administrators who rebook the deals (Carole Frank and others) on Credit's Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 3, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards to Carole Frank in giron-d/sent.
32:- Flipping ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books: Have EOL/TAGG book deals with ECC's master-swap counterparties straight to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book, with a daily exception report, instead of manual search-and-flip requests.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals', which cites the same Giron messages.
33-- Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report: Put the West desk's rebook handler (Carole Frank) or a desk mailbox directly on Credit's daily Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every business day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 4, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards in giron-d/sent.

13	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
14	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
15	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
16	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
17	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
18	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
19	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
20	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
21	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
22	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. I rejected this proposal as a duplicate and did not save it. Nothing is wrong with the idea or with your rebuilt evidence; it is simply already on the list.

**Why:** `decisions.md` already has this work saved as item 3, "Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals", at $364.65 a month. That entry:

- cites most of the same messages: giron-d/sent 108, 114, 195, 292, 360 and 407, plus 535 and 550.

It was saved while you were revising. Another critic has also already rejected a near-identical version ("Flipping ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books") as a duplicate of item 3.

More research would not change this, so the rejection has no research note. Saving yours as well would count the same savings twice. I didn't check your quotes, since the duplicate settles it.

If you have something the saved version lacks, add it to item 3 rather than saving a second proposal. Two parts of your work may be new:

TITLE: Auto-archive month-end P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for every gas book to a read-only auditor folder, instead of gathering them by hand for Arthur Andersen's monthly gas testing

TODAY
Every month Arthur Andersen (Sharon Smith, Mark Austin) emails the gas desk controllers (Kelly, Keiser, Giron, Baumbach and later others) a list of regions or books. For each, they ask for the P&L top page for the last day of the month and, where curve shift drives the P&L, top pages and Curve Shift Reports for the five largest days. Each controller forwards the request to his book admins, who find, print or copy the reports and send them back up. AA then chases anything missing. These are reports the risk system already produces every day. The work is retrieving, copying and routing them.
- The frequency is stated. corpus/giron-d/sent/201.eml (Feb 2001, Mark Austin, to 11 controllers and admins): "As part of our monthly testing, we review the monthly Natural Gas P & L Statement and identify specific regions for which we would like to review additional documentation... We are requesting that you supply the P & L top pages for the last day of the month for those regions that are applicable to you." Giron forwards it to 7 admins: "Please make sure this guy gets what he needs."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/516.eml (Nov 2000, Sharon Smith): "In order for us to complete our monthly gas testing, please provide the following items. P&L top sheet for the last day of August.  Additionally, if the majority of the P&L pertains to curve shift, please provide the P&L top pages for five of  the  largest days including the Curve Shift Reports." Six regions over two months are listed. Giron to 4 admins: "Please get this info to me and I will pass it on to AA."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/327.eml and 317.eml (Jan 2001): a request for 16 region-months (Nov and Dec). Giron is travelling, and AA presses: "Is there someone else that can direct us to?  I would like to get this information as soon as it is possible." Giron forwards to 3 admins, and then again to Kam Keiser.
- Requests have to be chased. corpus/giron-d/sent/583.eml (Oct 2000), subject "August P&L (2nd request)". It arrives with Gossett after the role change ("Darron has taken my position as west controller... Can you forward this to the appropriate book admin?"), and Giron forwards it: "Gather this info when you get a chance and give it to me." corpus/giron-d/sent/420.eml (Dec 2000): "we have not received the P&L top pages or curve shift reports for the following regions:  West Firm, FT Northwest and Mgmt. West." Giron: "Pull this together and then call Sharon so they can come get the copies."
- AA can't find the owners. corpus/giron-d/sent/299.eml (Jan 2001): "please direct me to the individual responsible for each of the desks listed below."

CHANGE
At each month-end close, a scheduled job saves the official last-day P&L top page and the daily top pages and curve-shift reports for every gas book into a dated, read-only folder that AA can open. The job also keeps a book-to-admin owner list in that folder. AA picks its sample straight from the folder and contacts the listed owner only to discuss P&L drivers.

AFTER
No forwarding chain, no hunting and copying, no second requests or "come get the copies" calls. Controllers and admins only spend time on the driver discussions, which are unchanged and not counted. The retrieval step disappears: AA opens a file that already exists rather than taking over the copying work, so nothing is passed on to someone else.

ESTIMATE (assumptions labelled)
Per month today, Enron staff only:
- Controllers read and forward the request: about 4 controllers × 5 min = 20 min.
- Admins pull top pages and curve-shift reports for the sampled regions: about 8 region-months a month (516 lists 6, 327 lists 16, 299 lists 6), assumed 15 min each = 120 min.
- Chasing missing items or second requests, rerouting after role changes (583, 420, 299, 317): about 20 min.
Total about 160 min.
After: set-up only, with no recurring retrieval beyond about 10 min to check the archive ran.
Saving about 150 min a month, about 2.5 h × $85, about $212 a month.
The frequency is monthly, as AA states ("our monthly testing"). The per-item minutes are assumptions.

No message I used tried to instruct the processor.

- corpus/giron-d/sent/327.eml and 317.eml (Jan 2001): a request for 16 region-months (Nov and Dec). Giron is travelling, and AA presses: "Is there someone else that can direct us to? - Requests have to be chased. corpus/giron-d/sent/583.eml (Oct 2000), subject "August P&L (2nd request)". CHANGE
At each month-end close, a scheduled job saves the official last-day P&L top page and the daily top pages and curve-shift reports for every gas book into a dated, read-only folder that AA can open. The job also keeps a book-to-admin owner list in that folder. AA picks its sample straight from the folder and contacts the listed owner only to discuss P&L drivers.

AFTER
No forwarding chain, no hunting and copying, no second requests or "come get the copies" calls. Controllers and admins only spend time on the driver discussions, which are unchanged and not counted. The retrieval step disappears: AA opens a file that already exists rather than taking over the copying work, so nothing is passed on to someone else.

- Chasing missing items or second requests, rerouting after role changes (583, 420, 299, 317): about 20 min.
Total about 160 min.
After: set-up only, with no recurring retrieval beyond about 10 min to check the archive ran.
Saving about 150 min a month, about 2.5 h × $85, about $212 a month.

Please check this proposal against the archive in `corpus` and save it if it holds up.

TITLE: Build the monthly Enron Wholesale Services administrative-assistant roster from HR and directory data, instead of emailing a spreadsheet to every assistant each month for confirmation

TODAY
Jessica Ramirez (EWS Office of the Chairman) emails a spreadsheet (EEOC.xls) to the whole admin-assistant pool. Each person must check their own row (title, location, extension, fax, supervisor) and reply with corrections. She then folds the replies back into the list. The distribution itself is wrong: a non-assistant manager is on it and has to write back to be removed.
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/313.eml (9 Aug 2001), quoting Ramirez's message to 34 recipients: "On a monthly basis I will be verifying information such as your titles, locations, extension, fax numbers, & supervisors to help Office of the Chairman for Enron Wholesale Services keep track of all the Admin Assitants in the group." / "Please let me know if the information pertaining to you is correct on the list. If it is not, please forward me the correct info." / " << File: EEOC.xls >> "
- In the same file, Bill Williams III replies: "Please remove me from this list. I am not involved with the management of anyone in this pool."

The frequency is stated in the message: monthly.

CHANGE
Generate the roster each month straight from the HR system of record (title, supervisor, location) and the phone directory (extension, fax). Ramirez gets a refreshed file automatically. Assistants are asked nothing. Corrections happen where the data belongs (HR or directory updates), which already have to be made when someone moves. The distribution list is no longer needed, which also ends wrong-recipient replies like Williams's.

AFTER
The Office of the Chairman has a current list every month without 34 people opening a spreadsheet and replying, and without Ramirez merging replies.

ESTIMATE (assumptions labelled)
- Today, per month: 34 recipients each open the xls, find their row, check 5 fields and reply. Assumed 3 min each = 102 min. Ramirez reads the replies and updates the spreadsheet, assumed 45 min. Wrong-recipient handling (as in 313.eml), about 5 min.
- Total about 152 min a month.
- After: about 10 min for Ramirez to review the generated file.
- Saving about 142 min a month, about 2.4 h × $85, about $201 a month.
- No work moves to anyone else. HR and directory updates are made anyway when details change, so keeping that data current is not new work.
The per-person minutes are assumptions. The mail shows the request and its monthly frequency but no time figures.

No message I used tried to instruct the processor.

TITLE: Build the monthly Enron Wholesale Services administrative-assistant roster from HR and directory data, instead of emailing a spreadsheet to every assistant each month for confirmation

TODAY
Jessica Ramirez (EWS Office of the Chairman) emails a spreadsheet (EEOC.xls) to the whole admin-assistant pool. Each person must check their own row (title, location, extension, fax, supervisor) and reply with corrections. She then folds the replies back into the list. The distribution itself is wrong: a non-assistant manager is on it and has to write back to be removed.
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/313.eml (9 Aug 2001), quoting Ramirez's message to 34 recipients: "On a monthly basis I will be verifying information such as your titles, locations, extension, fax numbers, & supervisors to help Office of the Chairman for Enron Wholesale Services keep track of all the Admin Assitants in the group." / "Please let me know if the information pertaining to you is correct on the list. If it is not, please forward me the correct info." / " << File: EEOC.xls >> "
- In the same file, Bill Williams III replies: "Please remove me from this list. I am not involved with the management of anyone in this pool."

The frequency is stated in the message: monthly.

CHANGE
Generate the roster each month straight from the HR system of record (title, supervisor, location) and the phone directory (extension, fax). Ramirez gets a refreshed file automatically. Assistants are asked nothing. Corrections happen where the data belongs (HR or directory updates), which already have to be made when someone moves. The distribution list is no longer needed, which also ends wrong-recipient replies like Williams's.

AFTER
The Office of the Chairman has a current list every month without 34 people opening a spreadsheet and replying, and without Ramirez merging replies.

ESTIMATE (assumptions labelled)
- Today, per month: 34 recipients each open the xls, find their row, check 5 fields and reply. Assumed 3 min each = 102 min. Ramirez reads the replies and updates the spreadsheet, assumed 45 min. Wrong-recipient handling (as in 313.eml), about 5 min.
- Total about 152 min a month.
- After: about 10 min for Ramirez to review the generated file.
- Saving about 142 min a month, about 2.4 h × $85, about $201 a month.
- No work moves to anyone else. HR and directory updates are made anyway when details change, so keeping that data current is not new work.
The per-person minutes are assumptions. The mail shows the request and its monthly frequency but no time figures.

For 1/01, the sale would be for $886,638.60 (the 12/00 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).  For 2/01, the sale would be for $839,008.29 (the 1/01 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).

This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward:
The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly.
The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out.
The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM.

Once this is done, the A/R balance for GLO will be cleared, the margin will be on the ENA Wellhead book, and the intercompany transactions will move the money from EGM to HPL.  This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value.  We should also know the value of the crude oil so that we can flash the sale from ENA to EGM.  If you have any questions or see a better way to do this, please let me know.  Thanks.
